assessments.title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
assessments.description: Core concepts: supervised learning, splits, overfitting, and evaluation.

questions.question: Why do we hold out a test set that the model never trains on?
options: To estimate performance on unseen data
To increase the number of features
questions.explanation: A held-out test set gives an unbiased estimate of how the model generalizes to new data.

questions.question: A model gets 99% accuracy on training data but 62% on the test set. This is a classic sign of:
questions.explanation: A large train-vs-test gap indicates the model memorized the training data instead of learning general patterns.

questions.question: A very simple model that consistently misses important patterns has:
questions.explanation: High bias means the model is too simple to capture the underlying relationship.

questions.question: For a heavily imbalanced classification problem (99% class A, 1% class B), why is accuracy misleading?
options: Accuracy is always wrong for classification
A model predicting only class A still gets 99% accuracy while learning nothing about class B
Accuracy cannot be computed with more than two classes
questions.explanation: Accuracy on imbalanced data rewards trivial majority-class predictions; precision/recall or AUC are more informative.

assessments.title: Classification Modeling
assessments.description: Metrics, thresholds, imbalance, and decision boundaries.

questions.question: Precision measures:
options: Of all actual positives, how many were predicted correctly
Of all predicted positives, how many are actually positive
The fraction of all data predicted positive
The fraction of negatives correctly rejected
questions.explanation: Precision = TP / (TP + FP). It answers: when we predict positive, how often are we right?

questions.question: An ROC-AUC of 0.5 means the model:
options: Performs no better than random guessing
questions.explanation: AUC = 0.5 corresponds to random ranking of positive vs negative instances.

questions.question: Select techniques that help with class imbalance:
options: Using class weights in the loss function
Deleting all data from the minority class
Reporting precision, recall, and F1 instead of raw accuracy
questions.explanation: Resampling, class weights, and better metrics all address imbalance; deleting minority data destroys information.

questions.question: A logistic regression on two features produces a straight decision boundary. The data is clearly separated by a circle. What is the best first step?
options: Add polynomial feature combinations (e.g., x1^2, x1*x2)
Collect more of the same data
Switch to a neural network with 50 layers immediately
questions.explanation: Adding nonlinear feature transformations lets a linear model fit nonlinear boundaries — a simple, interpretable fix.

questions.question: RMSE penalizes large errors more heavily than MAE because:
options: It squares errors before averaging, amplifying outliers
questions.explanation: Squaring errors gives disproportionate weight to large residuals, making RMSE sensitive to outliers.

questions.question: Ridge (L2) regularization helps by:
options: Adding a penalty on the sum of squared coefficients to shrink them
questions.explanation: L2 penalty shrinks coefficients toward zero, reducing variance and overfitting.

questions.question: For a linear regression y = 50 + 3·x, the coefficient 3 means:
options: A one-unit increase in x is associated with a 3-unit increase in y, all else equal
x explains exactly 3% of the variance
questions.explanation: The coefficient is the expected change in the target per unit change in the predictor, holding others fixed.

questions.question: R² = 0.9 for a regression model means:
options: The model explains 90% of the variance in the target
Predictions are within 10% of true values
questions.explanation: R² measures the proportion of target variance explained by the model relative to the mean baseline.

assessments.title: Deep Learning
assessments.description: Backpropagation, activations, optimizers, and training dynamics.

questions.question: Backpropagation computes:
options: The gradient of the loss with respect to every weight via the chain rule
questions.explanation: Backprop efficiently propagates loss gradients backward through the network using the chain rule.

questions.question: Why is ReLU preferred over sigmoid in hidden layers of deep networks?
options: It is cheaper and avoids vanishing gradients for positive inputs
It is bounded between 0 and 1 by design
It guarantees convergence in one epoch
It removes the need for a loss function
questions.explanation: ReLU's linear slope for positive inputs keeps gradients flowing, avoiding the saturation of sigmoid/tanh.

questions.question: A learning rate that is too high typically causes:
options: Oscillation or divergence of the loss
questions.explanation: Large steps can overshoot minima, causing the loss to oscillate or explode.

questions.question: Select techniques used to reduce overfitting in neural networks:
questions.explanation: Dropout, augmentation, and early stopping all regularize; removing validation data hides overfitting instead of fixing it.

questions.question: The Central Limit Theorem says that:
options: The distribution of sample means approaches a normal distribution as sample size grows
All raw data is normally distributed
The median always equals the mean
questions.explanation: Averages of many independent samples become approximately normal regardless of the underlying distribution.

questions.question: A p-value of 0.03 in a hypothesis test means:
options: There is a 3% chance the null hypothesis is true
Under the null hypothesis, results this extreme occur 3% of the time
questions.explanation: The p-value is the probability of observing data this extreme assuming the null hypothesis is true.

questions.question: A correlation of 0.9 between X and Y implies:
options: A strong linear association, but causation is not established
questions.explanation: Correlation measures association, not causation; confounding variables may explain the link.

questions.question: You compare two website designs and want to know if the conversion difference is real. Which approach is most appropriate?
options: Run an A/B test and compute a confidence interval for the conversion difference
Pick the design with the higher raw conversion after one hour
Ask five colleagues which design they prefer
Assume the difference is real if it is bigger than 1%
questions.explanation: A properly powered experiment with confidence intervals accounts for sampling variability.

questions.question: Which data structure stores unique elements and has O(1) average membership checks?
questions.explanation: Sets are hash-based, giving fast membership tests and automatic deduplication.

questions.question: What does [x*x for x in range(4)] produce?
questions.explanation: It squares each of 0, 1, 2, 3, yielding [0, 1, 4, 9].

questions.question: What does a function with 'return' missing at the end return?
questions.explanation: Python implicitly returns None when no return statement is reached.

questions.question: The '__init__' method in a Python class is:
options: The constructor-like initializer called when an instance is created
questions.explanation: __init__ initializes instance attributes when the object is instantiated.

assessments.title: Pandas & Data Wrangling
assessments.description: Filtering, grouping, joins, and missing data.

questions.question: Which expression selects rows where column 'age' is greater than 30?
questions.explanation: Boolean masking with df[boolean_series] filters rows.

questions.question: df.groupby('city')['sales'].mean() computes:
options: The city with the highest sales
A pivot table of sales by year
questions.explanation: groupby splits by city, then mean() aggregates the sales column per group.

questions.question: Which is generally the LEAST safe way to handle missing values?
options: Imputing with the median when appropriate
Dropping the entire column because it has missing values
questions.explanation: Dropping a whole column discards potentially valuable information; imputation or indicators are usually better.

questions.question: An inner join between two DataFrames:
options: Keeps rows with matching keys in both frames
Keeps all rows from the left frame
Keeps all rows from both frames
questions.explanation: Inner join returns only the intersection of keys between the two frames.

questions.question: Which join returns all rows from the left table and matched rows from the right?
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps every row of the left table, filling NULLs where there is no match.

questions.question: SELECT department, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY department; returns:
questions.explanation: GROUP BY collapses rows into groups; COUNT(*) counts rows within each group.

questions.question: What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING?
options: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation
questions.explanation: WHERE applies to raw rows; HAVING applies to aggregated results.

questions.question: A correlated subquery:
options: References columns from the outer query and runs per outer row
Runs once and caches the result
questions.explanation: Correlated subqueries depend on the outer row, so they are evaluated per row.

questions.question: A Docker image is best described as:
options: A read-only template used to create containers
questions.explanation: Images are immutable layers; containers are runnable instances of an image.

questions.question: In a Dockerfile, which instruction copies files from the build context into the image?
questions.explanation: COPY (and ADD) copy local files into the image filesystem.

questions.question: Why use a Docker volume for a database container?
options: To persist data beyond the container's lifecycle
To expose ports to the internet
questions.explanation: Containers are ephemeral; volumes keep data safe when containers are recreated.

questions.question: Docker Compose is mainly used to:
options: Define and run multi-container applications with one file
questions.explanation: docker-compose.yml declares services, networks, and volumes for multi-container apps.

assessments.title: Cybersecurity Fundamentals
assessments.description: CIA triad, threats, defense in depth, risk.

questions.question: The 'A' in the CIA triad stands for:
questions.explanation: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability — the three pillars of information security.

questions.question: Phishing is best classified as a:
questions.explanation: Phishing manipulates people into revealing credentials or installing malware.

questions.question: Select layers that belong to a defense-in-depth strategy:
options: Relying on a single password for everything
questions.explanation: Multiple independent controls reduce the impact of any single failure.

questions.question: An organization discovers a critical vulnerability in an internet-facing system. The best first response is:
options: Assess exposure, then apply the patch or compensating controls urgently
Ignore it until the next maintenance window in six months
Email all employees to warn them
questions.explanation: Risk = likelihood × impact; a critical internet-facing flaw demands immediate mitigation.

assessments.title: Web Application Security
assessments.description: Injection, XSS, CSRF, and authentication flaws.

questions.question: SQL injection is prevented primarily by:
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries separate data from code so user input cannot alter SQL structure.

questions.question: Stored XSS occurs when:
options: Malicious script is saved on the server and executed in other users' browsers
A user refreshes the page too quickly
questions.explanation: Stored XSS persists attacker-controlled script that later executes for victims.

questions.question: CSRF tokens protect against:
options: A malicious site submitting requests using the victim's authenticated session
questions.explanation: Tokens verify the request originated from the legitimate site, not a third party.

questions.question: The safest way to store passwords is:
options: A salted, slow hash such as bcrypt/argon2
questions.explanation: Salted slow hashes resist brute force and rainbow tables.

assessments.title: AWS Core Services
assessments.description: Compute, storage, IAM, and pricing concepts.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides resizable virtual servers?
questions.explanation: EC2 offers virtual machines with configurable instance types.

questions.question: S3 is best used for:
options: Object storage at scale with high durability
Block storage attached to a single EC2 instance
questions.explanation: S3 stores objects (files) with 99.999999999% durability.

questions.question: The principle of least privilege in IAM means:
options: Grant users only the permissions they need to do their job
Grant everyone admin access for convenience
Use root credentials for all automation
questions.explanation: Least privilege minimizes the blast radius of compromised credentials.

questions.question: A workload that runs 24/7 and needs consistent capacity is best priced with:
options: On-Demand for steady use, or Reserved Instances for significant savings
Spot Instances, which are guaranteed to never terminate
questions.explanation: Reserved/On-Demand suit steady workloads; spot is for interruptible, flexible jobs.

questions.question: The 'const' keyword declares a variable that:
options: Is always immutable even for objects
Is hoisted only in strict mode
questions.explanation: const blocks reassignment of the binding; object contents can still change.

questions.question: Which statement correctly awaits an asynchronous operation?
options: const data = await fetch(url); inside an async function
await is only valid outside functions
questions.explanation: await pauses an async function until the promise settles.

questions.question: document.querySelector('.card') returns:
options: The first element matching the CSS selector
An array of all matching elements
questions.explanation: querySelector returns the first match; querySelectorAll returns all matches.

questions.question: An arrow function (x) => x * 2 differs from function(x){ return x * 2 } in that it:
options: Has no own 'this' binding and implicitly returns the expression
questions.explanation: Arrow functions inherit 'this' lexically and can return expressions implicitly.
